iterations.title: World model in the control loop
iterations.question: Can a small JEPA-style world model improve grasp recovery?
iterations.evidence: 200 task attempts per controller across 5 conditions; missing-object stops were reported separately.
iterations.measure: JEPA planner 152/200 task successes; feedback 155/200.
iterations.detail: Prediction error improved only slightly over the hold-current estimate. The planner did not improve overall task completion, so feedback stayed the default.

iterations.title: Keep the grasp offset consistent
iterations.question: Can one offset from open descent through closure reduce ranking errors?
iterations.evidence: 720 matched trials; 6 conditions; 40 trials per condition and controller.
iterations.measure: Feedback 150/200; original JEPA and coherent-offset variant 145/200 each.
iterations.detail: The coherent variant cut planning calls from 146 to 41. It had no paired wins and 5 losses against feedback. The change did not improve success or produce a material speed gain.

iterations.title: Predict finger contact
iterations.question: Can measured finger force give a better grasp signal than the held score?
iterations.evidence: 240 training, 80 validation, 80 test scenes; 40 new ranking scenes and 1,000 branches.
iterations.measure: Test macro AP 0.585 vs 0.223; Brier 0.068 vs 0.138. Ranking top choice: 25/40 vs 27/40 unchanged.
iterations.detail: Prediction improved overall, but red-cylinder recall stayed low. Candidate AP was 0.778 for the head and 0.738 for the old score. The contact head stayed out of the controller.

iterations.title: Target red-cylinder contact
iterations.question: Does targeted tipped-cylinder and slip data improve the weak object class?
iterations.evidence: 103 training, 24 validation, 40 test scenes; then 20 ranking scenes and 40 independent scenes.
iterations.measure: Red-cylinder AP 0.777 vs V3 0.732. Independent ranking: 20/40 vs 22/40 unchanged.
iterations.detail: Recall at a 0.5 threshold improved from 7.2% to 29.8%, but calibration stayed weak. The fresh independent ranking did not beat the unchanged grasp.
iterations.result: Better red-cylinder prediction; no ranking gain

iterations.title: Learn to rank grasp candidates
iterations.question: Can a tiny model combine contact forecasts and candidate geometry?
iterations.evidence: 40 training, 20 validation, and 40 test scenes; plus 40 fresh replication scenes. 1,000 branches in each test.
iterations.measure: First test: 29/40 vs 26/40 unchanged. Replication: 27/40 vs 25/40. Combined: 56/80 vs 51/80.
iterations.detail: The 241-parameter reranker had candidate AP 0.816 and 0.832 across the two audits; unchanged grasp AP was 0.777 and 0.801. Paired results: 12 wins, 7 losses, 61 ties (exact sign p=0.359). V6 later tested it as a recovery proposal; that test showed no task-success gain.
iterations.result: Small consistent contact-ranking lead; not a control result

iterations.title: Guarded world-model proposal with feedback recovery
iterations.question: Can a bounded model proposal help after feedback detects an empty grasp?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched red-cylinder task trials across five conditions, plus 8 missing-object checks; 8 task trials per condition.
iterations.measure: Feedback 26/40; hybrid 26/40. Paired outcomes: 0 wins, 0 losses, 40 ties (exact sign p=1.000).
iterations.detail: Feedback acted first. On recovery, the frozen JEPA and V5 ranker proposed a bounded grasp offset. Finger checks, camera replanning, and retries remained active. The ranker made 3 proposals during 17 retries; none changed task success. A feature audit found a contact-head channel mismatch in V5, so correct its inputs and retrain before another controller test.
iterations.result: No task-success gain; reranker features need correction

iterations.title: Correct the reranker inputs
iterations.kind: Corrected offline model and controller test
iterations.question: Does the corrected red-cylinder contact channel improve grasp ranking?
iterations.evidence: 40 fresh offline scenes with 1,000 branches; then 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Offline contact choice: 29/40 vs 27/40 unchanged. Controller: feedback and hybrid both 25/40.
iterations.detail: The corrected reranker used contact-head channel 3 for the red cylinder and removed the simulator-only tipped label. The controller had 0 wins, 0 losses, and 40 ties. Better contact ranking did not improve task success.
iterations.result: Better contact choice; no task gain

iterations.title: Fine-tune on fallen-cylinder scenes
iterations.question: Can extra fallen-object demonstrations improve the VLA policy?
iterations.evidence: 240 training scenes, 60 validation scenes, and 40 matched task trials.
iterations.measure: Tipped waypoint error fell from 7.15 mm to 6.08 mm. Task success fell from 21/40 to 19/40.
iterations.detail: The adapted policy improved its tipped-scene waypoint metric but lost two task successes overall. It had 1 win and 3 losses against the base policy. Keep the base policy as the default.
iterations.result: Better waypoint metric; worse task result

iterations.title: Retry with the last valid visual plan
iterations.question: Can a saved visual target help when the camera briefly loses the object?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks on fresh seeds.
iterations.measure: Feedback 21/40; hybrid 21/40. The fallback ran 30 times.
iterations.detail: The first low-confidence view still stopped the controller. A saved target was used only after a prior valid view and during bounded recovery. It did not add a successful task.

iterations.title: Test visual routing to the adapted policy
iterations.question: Can a small visual gate select the adapted policy only for a fallen object?
iterations.evidence: Three gates tested on 40 fresh tipped and 40 fresh upright scenes each.
iterations.measure: Best tipped-object recall was 5%, with a 2.5% false-positive rate. No controller test was run.
iterations.detail: A linear gate, a small MLP, and a crop classifier all missed most fallen cylinders. The gate did not meet the fixed validation limit, so the routed model stayed out of the controller.

iterations.title: Relax the proposal gate
iterations.question: Will more frequent recovery proposals turn contact ranking into task gains?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Feedback and hybrid both 24/40; 0 wins and 0 losses.
iterations.detail: The permissive gate accepted all four non-default proposals. None changed the final task result. The missing-object safe-stop rate stayed 7/8 for both.

iterations.title: Use the reranker on the first grasp
iterations.question: Can a grasp proposal help before the first failed attempt?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched task trials and 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Feedback and hybrid both 23/40; 2 wins, 2 losses, and 36 ties.
iterations.detail: The ranker changed 41 grasp commands. Two feedback failures became successes, but two successful feedback trials became failures. The net task result was unchanged.

iterations.title: Rank grasps by complete task success
iterations.question: Does a ranker trained on full pick, lift, and place outcomes improve the controller?
iterations.evidence: Offline: 12/40 vs 4/40 successful grasp choices. Primary controller test: 30/40 vs 26/40. Independent replication: 27/40 vs 25/40.
iterations.measure: Across 80 matched trials: V13 57/80; feedback 51/80. Paired results: 11 wins, 5 losses, and 64 ties (exact p=0.210).
iterations.detail: Both fresh seed ranges favored V13. The combined gain is 6 tasks, but the paired test is small and does not establish a reliable effect. Missing-object safe stops were 15/16 for both controllers. Keep testing in simulation before any real-arm use.

iterations.title: Plan from the parked camera view
iterations.question: Can the controller skip its initial probe-and-return without reducing task success?
iterations.evidence: 40 matched hybrid task trials on the same fresh seeds; plus 8 missing-object checks.
iterations.measure: Original and direct-approach hybrid both completed 21/40 tasks. Paired outcomes: 0 wins, 0 losses, 40 ties. Inference calls fell from 122 to 89.
iterations.detail: V14 follows the first camera plan from the parked pose. It skips the first approach, retreat, and second pregrasp inference. Finger checks, retries, and the post-lift camera replan remain active. Both controllers stopped safely in 8/8 missing-object checks. Mean control time did not improve: 2.06 s for the original and 2.19 s for V14.

iterations.title: Run trials on the articulated B601-RS arm
iterations.question: Can a joint-limited pick-and-place run on the B601-RS model without the Panda surrogate?
iterations.evidence: 12 seeded red-cube trials with small randomized starts; 3 selected videos. The teacher reads simulator state.
iterations.measure: 12/12 placements; all six arm joints stayed within their URDF limits. Speed and gripper conversion still need calibration.
iterations.detail: The trials load Seeed’s B601-RS URDF in PyBullet, use its six arm joints and two prismatic fingers, and move with quintic joint-space profiles. The reference peaks at up to 2.25 rad/s, above Seeed’s 1.50 rad/s web target limit; the finger motor-to-width conversion is not reproduced. This validates the articulated simulator path, not a learned VLA or a controller-faithful speed and gripper stack.

iterations.title: Randomize three cube starts
iterations.question: Can the articulated arm sort three colored cubes from randomized starts?
iterations.evidence: 5 fresh seeds; a 4-by-7 start grid; randomized yaw and pick order; 35 mm placement tolerance.
iterations.measure: 3/5 complete sorts; 12/15 cubes placed; 14 recovery attempts.
iterations.detail: The broad workspace exposed edge-of-reach and transfer failures. Some cubes moved off the table. Retries could not recover them. The teacher reads exact simulator state.

iterations.title: Narrow the randomized start band
iterations.question: Does removing the far start positions make the three-cube task reliable?
iterations.evidence: 5 fresh seeds; 3-by-7 start grid; randomized yaw and pick order.
iterations.measure: 1/5 complete sorts; 11/15 cubes placed; 9 recovery attempts.
iterations.detail: A narrower table region alone did not fix failures. The old 220 mm approach pose had 50–88 mm IK position error in the tested grid.

iterations.title: Lower the approach and carry poses
iterations.question: Does a lower waypoint reduce B601 inverse-kinematics error?
iterations.evidence: 5 fresh seeds; same three-cube sort and 35 mm placement check.
iterations.measure: 2/5 complete sorts; 10/15 cubes placed.
iterations.detail: A 140 mm approach reduced the IK pose error. Lowering the carry pose as well did not improve sorting. The selected replay shows cubes displaced during the transfer sequence.
iterations.result: Better IK fit; task still unreliable

iterations.title: Keep transfers inside the core workspace
iterations.question: Can a smaller start area and raised carry pose avoid table collisions?
iterations.evidence: 5 fresh seeds; x positions capped at 310 mm; 35 mm placement check.
iterations.measure: 1/5 complete sorts; 9/15 cubes placed.
iterations.detail: This combination did not solve the problem. Some objects were knocked off the table. The next test returns the arm to its folded pose between picks.

iterations.title: Return to the folded pose between picks
iterations.question: Does returning to a known joint pose reduce collisions between picks?
iterations.evidence: 12 fresh seeds; 36 cube placements; randomized yaw and pick order.
iterations.measure: 9/12 complete sorts; 31/36 cubes placed; 23 recovery attempts.
iterations.detail: The arm retracts to its folded joint pose after each placement. This gave the best complete-sort rate so far. The batch still has three failed tasks and uses a scripted teacher.

iterations.title: Remove edge starts and avoid no-op starts
iterations.question: Can a reachable start band improve object placement without reducing the task?
iterations.evidence: 12 fresh seeds; starts stay at least 75 mm from their matching pads; 35 mm placement check.
iterations.measure: 9/12 complete sorts; 33/36 cubes placed; 12 recovery attempts.
iterations.detail: The full-sort count matches V6, while two more cubes reached their pads. This is the strongest object-level result so far. The batches are unpaired, so the difference is not a statistical claim.

iterations.title: Increase start density
iterations.question: How does a denser start area affect the B601 sorting task?
iterations.evidence: 12 fresh seeds; 18 candidate start positions; randomized yaw and pick order.
iterations.measure: 6/12 complete sorts; 29/36 cubes placed; 25 recovery attempts.
iterations.detail: The denser, smaller start area reduced performance. This is useful evidence about the current motion limits, not a model gain.

iterations.title: Check the grasp before transferring
iterations.question: Can a simulated lift check stop unsafe transfers after a missed grasp?
iterations.evidence: 12 fresh seeds; the teacher checks cube height and position before crossing the table.
iterations.measure: 9/12 complete sorts; 31/36 cubes placed; 13 failed-grasp checks.
iterations.detail: The guard did not raise full-sort success above V6 or V7. It is a useful failure check, but the randomized task still needs better motion planning and a reliable B601 gripper model.

iterations.title: Clear a barrier during three-cube sorting
iterations.question: Can the current scripted motion transfer three cubes across a solid tabletop barrier?
iterations.evidence: 12 seeds; each trial randomizes three cube starts, yaw, and pick order. Seed 610000 was reused from the initial wall-height check.
iterations.measure: 8/12 complete sorts; 30/36 cubes placed within 35 mm.
iterations.detail: A 45 mm wall separates every start from its matching pad. The teacher uses a 200 mm carry waypoint and up to two retries per cube. Seed 610000 was used to check an earlier, taller wall before this batch was fixed; the other 11 seeds were not used in that check. The open-table V7 batch scored 9/12 and 33/36 on different seeds, so these are not paired results. This is scripted simulation evidence, not a policy gain.

iterations.evidence: 12 trials, matched held-out seeds; training used 6,489 samples from 160 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/12 full sorts; 0/36 cubes. Teacher 5/12 sorts; 26/36 cubes.
iterations.detail: 96 px images; all demonstrations. The selected checkpoint is epoch 38 with 130,968 parameters and 0.45 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success.

iterations.question: Can this change improve the small policy's real sorting results?
iterations.evidence: 24 trials, 2 paired held-out seed groups; training used 2,672 samples from 80 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/24 full sorts; 1/72 cubes. Teacher 13/24 sorts; 58/72 cubes.
iterations.detail: Overhead camera; Cartesian waypoints. The selected checkpoint is epoch 37 with 426,774 parameters and 1.34 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success.

iterations.title: BC V8 · Add 40 episodes of DAgger corrections
iterations.question: Can teacher corrections on policy-visited states improve sorting?
iterations.evidence: 12 trials, matched held-out seeds; training used 3,440 samples from 112 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/12 full sorts; 0/36 cubes. Teacher 5/12 sorts; 26/36 cubes.
iterations.detail: Add 40 episodes of DAgger corrections. The selected checkpoint is epoch 34 with 426,774 parameters and 1.37 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The correction set had 40 episodes and 0 complete teacher-guided sorts; 768 correction samples entered training.

iterations.title: BC V9 · Add camera-derived cube and pad coordinates
iterations.question: Can camera-derived target features improve cube placement?
iterations.evidence: 36 trials, 3 paired held-out seed groups; training used 2,672 samples from 80 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/36 full sorts; 14/108 cubes. Teacher 21/36 sorts; 90/108 cubes.
iterations.detail: Add camera-derived cube and pad coordinates. The selected checkpoint is epoch 36 with 427,798 parameters and 1.77 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. This is an early object-level gain; neither V7 nor V9 completed a full sort in these 24 trials.

iterations.title: BC V10 · Combine camera-derived targets with DAgger
iterations.question: Do camera-derived targets and DAgger corrections work better together?
iterations.evidence: 24 trials, 2 paired held-out seed groups; training used 3,440 samples from 112 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/24 full sorts; 8/72 cubes. Teacher 13/24 sorts; 58/72 cubes.
iterations.detail: Combine camera-derived targets with DAgger. The selected checkpoint is epoch 28 with 427,798 parameters and 1.48 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The correction set had 40 episodes and 0 complete teacher-guided sorts; 768 correction samples entered training. Combining the visual cues with DAgger did not improve V9 overall: both placed 8/72 cubes and completed 0/24 full sorts. On the fresh seed group, V10 placed 3/36 cubes and V9 placed 6/36.

iterations.title: BC V11 · Correct overhead image yaw handedness
iterations.question: Does correcting the overhead camera's yaw direction improve face-aligned grasps?
iterations.evidence: 120 trials, 10 paired held-out seed groups; training used 2,672 samples from 80 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/120 full sorts; 72/360 cubes. Teacher 80/120 sorts; 311/360 cubes.
iterations.detail: Correct overhead image yaw handedness. The selected checkpoint is epoch 39 with 427,798 parameters and 1.91 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The overhead image-angle feature previously reversed world yaw. After correcting it, V11 placed 27/108 cubes across 36 paired seeds; V9 placed 14/108 on those same seeds. Neither completed a full sort. The paired trial sign test is promising but not conclusive (15 wins, 6 losses, 15 ties; p = 0.078).

iterations.title: BC V12 · Add corrections from V11-visited states
iterations.question: Can teacher corrections on V11-visited states improve grasping?
iterations.evidence: 36 trials, 3 paired held-out seed groups; training used 3,440 samples from 112 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/36 full sorts; 23/108 cubes. Teacher 21/36 sorts; 90/108 cubes.
iterations.detail: Add corrections from V11-visited states. The selected checkpoint is epoch 32 with 427,798 parameters and 2.06 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The correction set had 40 episodes and 0 complete teacher-guided sorts; 768 correction samples entered training. V12 added 768 teacher corrections from 40 V11-visited episodes. It placed 23/108 cubes across the same 36 paired seeds, compared with V11's 27/108. Neither completed a full sort; there were 11 V12-favored trials, 11 V11-favored trials, and 14 ties. DAgger did not improve the result.

iterations.title: BC V13 · Train on successful teacher episodes only
iterations.question: Does filtering to successful teacher sorts improve the learned policy?
iterations.evidence: 36 trials, 3 paired held-out seed groups; training used 1,632 samples from 56 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/36 full sorts; 4/108 cubes. Teacher 21/36 sorts; 90/108 cubes.
iterations.detail: Train on successful teacher episodes only. The selected checkpoint is epoch 38 with 427,798 parameters and 2.21 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. Training only on 56 successful demonstration episodes lowered validation waypoint error, but placed just 4/108 cubes across the same 36 paired seeds. V11 placed 27/108. The lower waypoint error did not predict task success.

iterations.title: BC V14 · Weight grasp-phase waypoint errors 3×
iterations.question: Does extra training weight on grasp phases improve object placements?
iterations.evidence: 36 trials, 3 paired held-out seed groups; training used 2,672 samples from 80 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/36 full sorts; 13/108 cubes. Teacher 21/36 sorts; 90/108 cubes.
iterations.detail: Weight grasp-phase waypoint errors 3×. The selected checkpoint is epoch 40 with 427,798 parameters and 2.12 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. Training multiplied descend, close, and lift waypoint loss by 3. On the same 36 held-out seeds, V14 placed 13/108 cubes and V11 placed 27/108; neither completed a full sort. V14 had more placements in 4 trials, fewer in 13, and tied in 19 (exact paired sign test p = 0.049). The grasp-phase weighting reduced task performance, so V11 remains the lead policy.

iterations.title: BC V15 · Weight carry, place, and release errors 3×
iterations.question: Does extra training weight on carry, place, and release phases improve sorting?
iterations.evidence: 36 trials, 3 paired held-out seed groups; training used 2,672 samples from 80 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 0/36 full sorts; 5/108 cubes. Teacher 21/36 sorts; 90/108 cubes.
iterations.detail: Weight carry, place, and release errors 3×. The selected checkpoint is epoch 39 with 427,798 parameters and 3.56 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. Training multiplied carry, place, and release waypoint loss by 3. On the same 36 held-out seeds, V15 placed 5/108 cubes and V11 placed 27/108; neither completed a full sort. V15 had more placements in 3 trials, fewer in 19, and tied in 14 (exact paired sign test p = 0.00086). Delivery-phase weighting reduced task performance.

iterations.title: BC V16 · Add 100 fresh teacher demonstration episodes
iterations.question: Do 100 fresh teacher episodes improve policy generalization?
iterations.evidence: 120 trials, 10 paired held-out seed groups; training used 5,424 samples from 160 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 1/120 full sorts; 109/360 cubes. Teacher 80/120 sorts; 311/360 cubes.
iterations.detail: Add 100 fresh teacher demonstration episodes. The selected checkpoint is epoch 40 with 427,798 parameters and 3.24 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The model adds 80 training episodes from a fresh 100-episode set; its validation split remains unchanged. Across 120 matched held-out seeds, V16 placed 109/360 cubes and completed 1/120 full sorts. V11 placed 72/360 cubes and completed none. V16 had more placements in 49 trials, fewer in 17, and tied in 54 (exact paired sign test p = 0.00010).

iterations.title: BC V17 · Add V16-state teacher corrections
iterations.question: Do teacher corrections from V16 policy states improve the expanded-data model?
iterations.evidence: 240 trials, 20 paired held-out seed groups; training used 6,192 samples from 192 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 12/240 full sorts; 244/720 cubes. Teacher 164/240 sorts; 629/720 cubes.
iterations.detail: Add V16-state teacher corrections. The selected checkpoint is epoch 23 with 427,798 parameters and 2.10 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. V17 adds 768 teacher corrections from 40 V16-visited episodes to the V16 training data. Across 120 matched held-out seeds, V17 placed 125/360 cubes and completed 5/120 full sorts; V16 placed 109/360 and completed 1/120. V17 had more placements in 47 trials, fewer in 40, and tied in 33 (exact paired sign test p = 0.520). V17 has the best observed count, but its gain over V16 is not conclusive.

iterations.title: BC V18 · Gate large policy errors with teacher takeovers
iterations.question: Can error-triggered teacher takeovers make DAgger data more useful?
iterations.evidence: 240 trials, 20 paired held-out seed groups; training used 7,152 samples from 232 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 14/240 full sorts; 261/720 cubes. Teacher 164/240 sorts; 629/720 cubes.
iterations.detail: Gate large policy errors with teacher takeovers. The selected checkpoint is epoch 18 with 427,798 parameters and 1.89 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The correction set had 50 episodes and 9 complete teacher-guided sorts; 960 correction samples entered training. V18 adds 960 intervention-guided correction samples from 50 episodes, including 9 complete sorts. Across 120 matched seeds, V18 placed 131/360 cubes and completed 6/120 full sorts. V17 placed 125/360 cubes and completed 5/120. V18 had 41 wins, 35 losses, and 44 ties (exact paired sign test p = 0.567). By color, green placements rose from 28 to 44, while blue placements fell from 52 to 39. This is the highest observed count, but the gain over V17 is not conclusive.

iterations.title: BC V19 · Weight blue-cube instruction samples 1.5 times
iterations.question: Does weighting blue-cube instructions improve the balance across colors?
iterations.evidence: 120 trials, 10 paired held-out seed groups; training used 7,152 samples from 232 episodes.
iterations.measure: Policy 14/120 full sorts; 150/360 cubes. Teacher 84/120 sorts; 318/360 cubes.
iterations.detail: Weight blue-cube instruction samples 1.5 times. The selected checkpoint is epoch 24 with 427,798 parameters and 4.73 ms CPU inference per action. Waypoint scores are in the data file; they do not replace task success. The correction set had 50 episodes and 9 complete teacher-guided sorts; 960 correction samples entered training. On 120 fresh matched seeds, V19 placed 150/360 cubes and completed 14/120 full sorts. V18 placed 130/360 and completed 8/120. V19 had 41 wins, 30 losses, and 49 ties (exact sign test p = 0.235); this gain is uncertain. Against V17, V19 placed 150/360 versus 119/360 (p = 0.028). By color against V18, placements were red 50 vs 47, blue 55 vs 50, and green 45 vs 33. The V19 lead over V17 is promising, but more fresh tests are needed to confirm it. On a separate confirmation set, V19 placed 145/360 cubes and completed 9/120 sorts; V18 placed 124/360 and completed 9/120. The paired comparison was 49 wins, 34 losses, and 37 ties (p = 0.124). Neither policy had a joint-limit violation.

iterations.title: Teacher grasp height · 12-scene pilot
iterations.question: Does a higher pick waypoint improve stable grasps and placements?
iterations.evidence: 12 matched simulation scenes; one pick attempt per cube; face-aligned wrist yaw.
iterations.measure: 0.10 m: 33/36 cubes and 9/12 sorts. 0.08 m: 23/36 cubes and 2/12 sorts.
iterations.detail: The 0.10 m waypoint had 7 wins, 0 losses, and 5 ties by seed (exact p = 0.0156). It improved pilot task outcomes. Mean corner proximity changed from 0.469 to 0.444; most contacts still landed near the top or bottom rim. This is pilot evidence, not a learned-policy result.

iterations.title: BC V20 · Higher teacher pick height
iterations.question: Does training on a higher grasp waypoint improve the learned policy's contact and placement results?
iterations.evidence: 120 matched held-out simulation scenes; 5,440 training samples from 200 train episodes; contact audit enabled.
iterations.detail: V20 had 30 wins, 46 losses, and 44 ties by scene (exact paired sign test p = 0.085). Its observed count was lower by 34 cubes; this test does not show a clear difference at the 0.05 level. Mean contact-to-corner score improved from 0.594 to 0.537, but mean wrist-to-face yaw error rose from 14.20° to 16.06°. No-contact objects rose from 49 to 62. Most contacts remained near the top or bottom rim. The V20 set also used fewer training samples than V19, so this is not a clean test of grasp height alone. The teacher pilot did not translate into a learned-policy improvement. Next, hold the V19 data and grasp height fixed while testing extra yaw loss on grasp waypoints.

iterations.title: BC V22 · Camera-corrected grasp poses
iterations.question: Can calibrated overhead pixels improve the policy's grasp alignment?
iterations.evidence: 120 fresh matched held-out scenes; frozen V19 checkpoint; contact audit enabled.
iterations.detail: V22 had 60 wins, 26 losses, and 34 ties by scene (exact paired sign test p = 0.000317). Mean wrist-to-face yaw error fell from 14.86° to 7.04°. Objects with no finger contact fell from 64 to 21; mean corner proximity fell from 0.559 to 0.466. The first test's paired full-sort result was uncertain (20 wins, 11 losses, 89 ties; p = 0.150). Independent confirmation (seeds 674000–674119): V22 placed 219/360 cubes and completed 27/120 sorts; V19 placed 141/360 and completed 8/120. V22 had 67 placement wins, 16 losses, and 37 ties (p = 1.4e-08); full-sort outcomes were 26 wins, 7 losses, and 87 ties (p = 0.001). Yaw error fell from 16.20° to 7.58°; no-contact objects fell from 80 to 14.

iterations.title: BC V23 · Grasp-height adjustment
iterations.question: Does raising the close waypoint move finger contact toward the middle of a cube face?
iterations.evidence: 12 matched pilot scenes; fresh 120-scene test on new seeds.
iterations.measure: Pilot, 12 matched scenes: V22 18/36 cubes and 0/12 sorts; +10 mm 24/36 and 4/12; +20 mm 27/36 and 5/12.
iterations.detail: The +20 mm pilot comparison had 8 wins, 2 losses, and 2 ties (p = 0.109). The pilot is small and selected +20 mm only as a candidate for the fresh test. It did not show a clear contact-center gain. Fresh test, seeds 676000–676119: V23 placed 260/360 cubes and completed 47/120 sorts; V22 placed 226/360 and completed 31/120. Placement outcomes: 49 wins, 22 losses, 49 ties (p = 0.00182); full sorts: 31 wins, 15 losses, 74 ties (p = 0.026). Mean absolute contact height changed from 18.95 mm to 18.57 mm.

iterations.title: BC V21 · Grasp-yaw loss weight
iterations.question: Does extra yaw loss on grasp waypoints improve face alignment and sorting?
iterations.evidence: 120 fresh matched held-out simulation scenes; frozen V19 reference; contact audit enabled.
iterations.detail: V21 had 31 placement wins, 54 losses, and 35 ties (p = 0.017). Mean yaw error rose from 15.04° to 16.01°; objects with no finger contact rose from 55 to 97. The added yaw loss did not improve the task.
